house.description: Refundable sales and use tax exemption created for certain items and services purchased to repair property damage caused by natural disasters.

additions: Subd. 41.
Repairs following a natural disaster.
(a) The sale of the following items or service is exempt when the item or service is purchased to repair or remediate damage to property caused by a natural disaster:
(i) windows;
(ii) doors;
(iii) siding materials;
(iv) insulation;
(v) trusses, shingles, and other roofing materials;
(vi) power generators;
(vii) equipment used for sandbagging;
(viii) replacement parts for pumps, valves, and other small equipment;
(ix) plywood; and
(x) tree removal and other services related to hauling debris.
(b) The exemption under this subdivision applies only if:
(1) a natural disaster is declared by the federal government, or by a local official under section 12.29; and
(2) the purchase is made within two years of the disaster declaration.

(c) The tax on purchases exempt under this subdivision must be imposed and collected as if the rates under section 297A.62, subdivisions 1 and 1a, applied and then refunded in the manner provided in section 297A.75.
EFFECTIVE DATE.
This section is effective retroactively for sales and purchases made after May 31, 2025.

SALES TAX REFUNDS FOR EXEMPT PURCHASES TO REPAIR PROPERTY DAMAGE CAUSED BY NATURAL DISASTERS.

Refunds for eligible purchases under Minnesota Statutes, section 297A.67, subdivision 41, must not be issued until after June 30, 2026. Notwithstanding the requirement of Minnesota Statutes, section 297A.67, subdivision 41, paragraph (b), that purchases must be made within two years of the disaster to be exempt, refunds for eligible purchases for disasters declared between June 1, 2025, and January 31, 2026, may be issued for purchases made through December 31, 2027, or two years after the disaster, whichever is later.
EFFECTIVE DATE.
This section is effective the day following final enactment.
